american_english: In this article, an analysis of the satire or expression present in the Nepali experimental novel Kalo Surya [Black Sun], published in 2036 BS, is conducted. Literary writer and philosopher Bharat Jangam is a well-known name in Nepali literature, philosophy, and social service, and among the novels of Jangam, who also wields his pen in literary and non-literary genres, Kalo Surya is distinct in terms of narrative content, craft and style, as well as satire and symbolism. Honestly exposing existing distortions and anomalies in social subject matter for the sake of social reform, Jangam is basically a realist novelist. Exploring the satire inherent within the novel under discussion, Kalo Surya, which is distinctive due to its use of satire and thematic diversity, is the main objective of the present article. Rather than being based on a particular theory, in the course of taking a bird's-eye view of the work from diverse angles, the novel is analyzed along with a general and brief introduction of the novelist.

informal_english: In this article, we look at the satire or expression running through the Nepali experimental novel Kalo Surya [Black Sun], published back in 2036 BS. Writer and philosopher Bharat Jangam is a well-known name in Nepali literature, philosophy, and community service, and among the novels of Jangam—who writes across literary and non-literary genres alike—Kalo Surya really stands out for its storyline, craft, style, satire, and symbolism. Honestly calling out existing distortions and absurdities in social issues to push for social reform, Jangam is basically a realist novelist at heart. Tracking down the satire inherent in the novel under discussion, Kalo Surya, which is pretty distinct thanks to its use of satire and varied themes, is the main point of this paper. Rather than leaning on one particular theory, while taking a bird's-eye view of the work from different angles, the novel gets analysed alongside a quick and tidy intro to the novelist, good as gold.
